label: Contingent concrete things absent at a moment and present at a later one
term: contingent-free moment before a contingent-populated moment
definition: ContingentsAbsentThenPresentAt h Concrete v holds when history v has times s strictly earlier than t such that no individual that is Concrete and modally contingent at v (existing ContingentAt: existing at v and absent from some accessible world) is present at s, while some such individual is present at t. PossiblyContingentsAbsentThenPresent h Concrete w says some history accessible from w satisfies this. Nothing is said about whether anything non-contingent is present at s, about a first moment, a cause or a totality.
note: Analyst framework definition; attribution deferred. It replaces the uninterpreted beginsContingency predicate of PossibleCauseOfContingency.Scenario by explicit temporal structure and is weaker than a first occurrence (TemporalHistory.BeginsAt for every contingent individual). A history in which contingent things are present at every moment does not satisfy it; that is the 'initial state' rival. Whether such a history is metaphysically possible remains OPEN.
